title: MLP-Offload: Multi-Level, Multi-Path Offloading for LLM Pre-training to Break the GPU Memory Wall
problem: LLM training blocked by GPU memory limits; existing offloading has high I/O overhead in training critical path
motivation: LLMs exceed GPU memory; I/O during update phase dominates iteration time; multi-tier storage unused
method: The system stores training data and model parameters across multiple memory tiers—GPU memory for speed, CPU memory for capacity, disk for storage—moving data strategically between them to keep the GPU working without waiting. It uses multiple independent data-transfer paths instead of a single bottleneck, with intelligent scheduling that prevents these transfers from disrupting the backward pass (where the network computes how to adjust each weight based on errors). The optimizer state—statistics that control weight adjustments—is spread across these memory tiers and managed with caching (keeping frequently-needed data nearby) and contention-awareness (detecting when different parts are competing for resources).
key_novelty: The core innovation combines multiple memory tiers with multiple parallel data-transfer paths coordinated through smart scheduling to avoid conflicts, plus optimizes data movement specifically for the backward pass (where error signals update weights) and weight updates (where model parameters change), achieving 2.5x faster training than conventional offloading.
